analysis.title: GS Bartlett - GS TMT TODAY 11.17.26
key_insights: Futures mixed (Nasdaq +50bps, S&P flat, Russell -40bps) as markets absorb Jensen Huang's departure from NVDA. Focus is on US regulatory moves toward China.

New US restrictions on China's access to high-end AI chips aim to stop Chinese companies from renting NVDA chips outside the US and from obtaining processors through other countries. Reuters reports the Trump administration will press ahead with blocking imports of Chinese data center equipment.
US optical names (COHR, LITE, MRVL, CIEN) are +5-10% pre-market on the hawkish China stance. China tech is lower (BABA -3%).

NVDA reports after the close today (release 4:20pm ET, call 5pm). The GS desk expects a solid print and guide, with beat/raise expected and broadly stable gross margins. Positioning has cleaned up, with NVDA down $2T in market cap from mid-October.

Investors are watching NVDA for any reiteration of prior CY27 commentary (>70% revenue growth), changes to capital return (last quarter $20bn share repurchase), and broader AI comments. The desk thinks incremental clarity on Jensen is unlikely today.
Options imply an 8% NVDA move on the print, among the largest in about two years of quarterly results.

The FCC effort to ban imports of new models of Chinese optical transceivers faces more opposition than previously known. Amazon, Google and Meta lobbied against it, and US firms could need up to a decade to comply. Three additional people say it is moving forward.

NVDA formed a National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee, chaired by Suzanne Nora Johnson. Its national security and trade compliance teams report to the Committee and to Interim CEO Colette Kress.
Amazon's planned $17bn+ Ohio AI data center investment is threatened. Ohio voters backed 21 measures to slow data center development, and three Amazon projects are affected (FT).
GS Global Investment Research forecasts the S&P 500 at 8,700 by end-2027 (+17%), with EPS growth slowing from roughly 30% in 2026 to 18% in 2027.
GS base case holds the S&P 500 forward P/E near 18x, down 19% in 2026 and near its 10-year average. AI capex growth should begin to slow in 2027.

Asia fell after new US AI chip export controls hit Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand and Indonesia (Kioxia, Advantest, SoftBank, Hynix, Samsung, TSMC down 2-5%). Europe is lower (FTSE -70bps, DAX -65bps, CAC -65bps).
The 10-year Treasury yield is down slightly at 5.11%. Crude is up 50bps after yesterday's sell-off. VP Vance said the Iran war 'won't become a forever war'.
GS Korea tech research initiated a monthly HBM tracker. It shows an upward revision in SK Hynix HBM revenue and operating profit expectations.

NVDA last quarter included a $20bn share repurchase in the quarter (reported). Prior CY27 commentary was for >70% revenue growth.

Scheduled release today. The report gives no figure.
Earnings growth is expected to decelerate as AI capex growth slows.

Uncertainty around Nvidia leadership after Jensen Huang's departure, with limited clarity expected from the earnings call.
Local backlash against data center buildout, such as the Ohio ballot measures.
AI capex growth slowing in 2027, with the 2028 and later outlook for AI investment and margins highly uncertain.

geopolitical: New US restrictions on China's access to high-end AI chips, including renting NVDA chips outside the US and obtaining them through third countries.
The Trump administration plans to block imports of Chinese data center equipment, specifically optical transceivers (FCC).
US AI chip export control measures extended to Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand and Indonesia.
VP Vance said the war in Iran 'won't become a forever war'.
Reports on Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's affair with an alleged Chinese spy have fueled calls in Washington for a tougher stance on Chinese technology.
